title: Answer to Question: The Developments in Tunisia
text:
Answer to Question

The Developments in Tunisia

Some of the events that Tunisia has passed through in the recent period raise question marks over whether Tunisia's current subordination is on its way towards change or not. Among those events are the following:

- Tunisian media circles, especially the two newspapers "Tunis News" and "al-Wasat al-Tunisiyya", carried reports to the effect that Zine El Abidine has been afflicted with prostate cancer, from which there is no hope of recovery, and that he travelled secretly to Europe to receive treatment there.

- In the month of August 2005 the Tunisian diplomat Kamel Morjane, who had been working at the United Nations High Commission for Refugees, was appointed to head the Tunisian Ministry of Defence. After Kamel Morjane took up his work as minister, he began an accelerated diplomatic campaign, among which was the concluding of important agreements with America.

- In the month of February 2006 Donald Rumsfeld visited the countries of the Arab Maghreb, among them Tunisia, and in the same year Kamel Morjane made a visit to America.

- In 2007 the first visit outside Europe of Sarkozy, the new French prime minister, known for his closeness to America, was to the countries of the Arab Maghreb.

- In the past month of July/June a delegation of the American Congress visited Tunisia.

- At the end of the past month of July/June a group of leaders of the Tunisian Ennahda movement were released.

- Recently the assistant to the American Chief of Staff, Admiral Edmund Giambastiani, visited Tunisia last week and met with senior Tunisian officials, and a delegation of American officers followed him with a visit to Tunisia.

So does all of this mean that America has begun to establish a foothold for itself in Tunisia?

Answer

So that the answer becomes clear, we mention the following:

1 - Tunisia is one of the regions that are candidates for a struggle for influence among the colonialist powers, due to its strategic location and its particular features, in addition to the fact that it is considered one of the political laboratories of the Western states. It became subject to the influence of England after the French military colonialism left it.

After Habib Bourguiba was removed in 1987, having become senile and incapable of carrying out the tasks of ruling, Zine El Abidine Ben Ali succeeded him in ruling, and he, like his predecessor, maintained his absolute subordination to the English without hesitation.

2 - America exploited the tension in the relationship between Tunisia and Libya in 1988 and tried to exercise pressure and inducement on Zine El Abidine in order to penetrate Tunisia. It provided generous security aid to Tunisia worth 61 million dollars under the slogan of (deterring aggression), the intention of which was to induce the Tunisian President to ignite a front against Colonel Gaddafi and to stand with America against his regime. But Zine El Abidine Ben Ali soon appeared in his true colours, turned his back on America, and restored the improvement of his relations with Gaddafi. America thereafter reduced its support for Tunisia to the level of only 8 million dollars. Thus America did not succeed in penetrating Ben Ali's agency to Britain; rather, he continued as things had been in the era of his predecessor Bourguiba before..

3 - America made several efforts in December 1994 through what was called the "Mediterranean Dialogue" under the umbrella of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO), which it was able, after the collapse of the Soviet Union, to use in an extremely influential manner. It is worth pointing out that this "dialogue" includes Algeria, Egypt, ("Israel"), Jordan, Mauritania, Morocco and Tunisia, despite their not being members of NATO.

4 - In return, the European Union, during the Barcelona meeting in November 1995, gathered the member states of the European Union and the states surrounding the Mediterranean (Algeria, Egypt, ("Israel"), Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Syria, Tunisia, Turkey, the Palestinian Authority) through what was called the "EUROMED project". The European Union had spent on this project of its, in the period between 1995-2000, an amount of nine billion euros. At a later time a union was brought about between five southern European states (France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Malta) and five states of North Africa, among them the states of the Arab Maghreb (Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, Libya, Mauritania), which was given the name (5+5). This union concentrated its efforts on combating terrorism and illegal immigration, and this prevented America from being able to influence that region anew. For example, only 2% of American foreign trade and less than 1% of American foreign investment relate to this region.

5 - During this period also the regime of Zine El Abidine was able to repel the attempt of the former American President Bill Clinton to penetrate the Tunisian walls in 1995 CE, when the American Assistant Secretary of State at the time, Pelletreau, failed in his visit to Tunisia to incorporate the Tunisian regime among the regimes which agreed to proceed in the American security projects in North Africa.

6 - In 2000, when the American administration changed, the American view towards the region became sharper, and the level of its pressures on it rose in order to bring about a reform which was presented to the states of the region through the "Greater Middle East Project". Despite that, America was not able to reap tangible results.

7 - As for America's first success in a semi-penetration of the impregnable Tunisian security barrier, it was after the bombings of the eleventh of September in 2001 CE, when talk of establishing American military bases became a familiar matter. The newspaper (The Wall Street Journal) published on 10 June 2003 CE a report in which it cited official responsible persons in the Department of Defence as considering the possibility of establishing (semi-permanent) military bases in Tunisia, Algeria and Morocco, within the framework of the major modifications intended to be introduced to the (global deployment of American forces), among them plans relating to reducing the number of American forces stationed in Germany and moving them to other places.

Tunisian circles opposed to the regime abroad confirmed these reports and said that an American base is intended to be built in the Bizerte region, with one part of it in Sidi Ahmed to be used as an air base and another part of it in Bachater to be used as a naval base.

In recent years Tunisia has been participating in periodic security meetings, with the participation of the rest of the states of North Africa, with America, whose declared aim is combating terrorism and pursuing the gunmen of the al-Qaeda organisation in North Africa.

America exercised other pressures on the rulers of Tunisia so that they would provide support to it in Iraq. A report was issued on 30 December 2003 by the American Council on Foreign Relations entitled (Africa: Terrorism's Sanctuaries), in which Tunisia was listed, alongside Egypt and Algeria, among the states that represent a medium-range threat for the development of terrorist threats in them.

And the visits of Congressmen and American officials in the last two years are within this context, that is, pressure and inducement for the sake of penetration.

Nevertheless, these American pressures have not succeeded in dragging Tunisia into going along with America; rather, it does not go beyond being a tactic in the English manner of not clashing with America openly, but rather disturbing it practically from behind a curtain.

The English realise America's serious interest in Tunisia, indeed in the whole of North Africa. Therefore the English, just as they arranged the transfer of power from Bourguiba to his trusted man Zine El Abidine, are likewise now arranging in advance the possibility of the transfer of power from Zine El Abidine to a successor to him who will continue in subordination to the English, and at the same time they are presenting this designated successor to power after Zine El Abidine as not provocative or hostile to America, and by this they block the road to America's escalating pressures on Tunisia. Thus Britain's choice fell on Kamel Morjane to calm America's pressures, on the consideration that this man is more acceptable to America than Zine El Abidine. This is with the knowledge that Zine El Abidine's illness is not (advanced), and the possibility of his remaining until the end of his term in 2009 is a possibility that exists; but the purpose of waving Kamel Morjane as his successor is to calm America's pressures on Tunisia. This is an English tactic according to its traditional method of consolidating its influence in a country if it notices pressures on it. It is similar to what it did in preserving the Libyan regime when America's pressures on it increased: England instructed it to bow to America, give up armament, and incline towards surrender in the Lockerbie issue and pay the required compensation... and all of that to cut off the arguments before America for continuing the pressures on Gaddafi, or at least to calm them.

And this waving of Kamel Morjane, and that he is the successor to the sick Zine El Abidine whose time will not be long, especially as Britain has magnified the news of his illness as though he were in his final throes! is for the purpose mentioned above of blocking the road to America's pressures. To understand that well, we mention some information about Kamel Morjane, who occupies the Ministry of Defence:

1. Kamel Morjane is a capable diplomatic man.

2. Despite his fame resulting from his holding external posts, his active membership in the ruling party is not apparent.

3. He is tied by a bond of marriage, kinship and clan with the current head of state Zine El Abidine Ben Ali; both of them are from the city of Hammam Sousse, and Kamel Morjane's wife is the daughter of Zine El Abidine's sister. And Zine El Abidine, famous for the cunning of foxes and kneaded with the rancour of English politics, trusts Kamel Morjane; therefore he handed him an important post, namely the post of Minister of Defence.

4. Because of the external tasks he held for long years, he acquired fame and a distinguished standing in the international community.

5. As a result of his distance from the internal policies of the Tunisian state, his name was not stained by the crimes of the regime against the country and its people, despite his defending Tunisia in his speeches, especially those he delivered at the United Nations. Therefore, from this aspect, he can be accepted internationally and locally with ease and facility.

Thus the supposition that Kamel Morjane can be won over by America is a very weak supposition.

It has been noticed recently that Kamel Morjane is exerting all he can to use every means that appears to him in order to promote himself before the powers he sees will be against him, so that they accept him, his expertise, his international standing and his internal influence. The political offensive which Kamel Morjane has begun is full of reassuring messages about his person, and that he will not work against the international community and American interests in particular, hoping by that to be able to neutralise America from undertaking actions against him or placing obstacles before him.

This is about Kamel Morjane.

As for Sarkozy, whose first visit outside Europe was to the countries of the Arab Maghreb, no noticeable effect on a change of power in Tunisia appeared from that visit of his, as he concentrated in his visit on the "Mediterranean partnership", to the extent that Morocco refused Sarkozy's visit, excusing itself with excuses of no consideration. What is most likely is that his visit is in the category of strengthening French cultural influence, not in the category of exercising political influence over the Tunisian regime, and it is an extension of Sarkozy's tours in the regions of English influence and in coordination with the British themselves; it resembles his visit to Libya some time ago to a great extent.

As for the release of 21 political detainees at the end of the past month of July, following Sarkozy's speaking during his visit to Tunisia about human rights and political detainees: these detainees were released on the occasion of the fiftieth anniversary of the establishment of the Tunisian Republic, and the coupling of the release with that occasion distanced it from being a result of Sarkozy's visit. In any case, its political use is closer to (harmonising with) America's calls for human rights, reform and democracy than to being a response to Sarkozy, with the exception of the release of the human rights defender, the lawyer Mohammed Abbou, since Sarkozy had raised this matter during his meeting with Zine El Abidine Ben Ali. As for the other twenty who were released, they are members of the Ennahda movement, and they were set free under restrictions placed on them by the Tunisian Ministry of Justice.

In conclusion, we can say that Kamel Morjane was brought to the Ministry of Defence "early" on English instructions, to calm the American pressures on the regime in Tunisia and to be prepared, when necessary, to take over the presidency of the state without facing any surprises or internal or external obstacles; and this is like "cooking the feast on a very low fire".

Nevertheless, a conclusion can be reached to the effect that reforms are expected to be carried out in Tunisia (in harmony) with the American wish, even if they are not fully satisfying to it, in addition to taking improving steps regarding human rights... and the like. However, it is very early to say that America has brought about influence for itself in Tunisia or that it is about to bring about influence for itself there; that is, Tunisia is still of assured loyalty to the English and to the Europeans, and the Tunisian security wall remains a solid defensive line against the American attempts at penetration. As long as the military and the security agencies remain cohesive under the leadership of the agents of the English, it is difficult for the American attempts to succeed in breaking that resisting wall.

21 Sha'ban 1428 AH

03 September 2007 CE
